bull.b: TTM operating cash flow and near-$1.8B free cash flow provide durable financial flexibility: they support debt service, large repurchases and a growing dividend, and fund investment in stores and digital. Strong recurring FCF also cushions cyclical retail volatility and underpins capital returns policy.

Coach’s strong global volume and AUR gains reflect durable brand power and pricing leverage. Rapid customer adds (millions in the quarter) and accelerated Gen Z acquisition indicate sustainable cohort renewal, higher lifetime value potential, and a stronger DTC channel that preserves margin and customer data over time.

Material gross- and operating-margin gains reflect improved mix, pricing and cost execution. Management’s raised margin guidance signals lasting structural improvements (product mix, operational expansion and SG&A leverage) that can sustain higher profitability and free cash generation even as growth normalizes.

bear.b: Very high debt-to-equity materially increases financial risk and reduces balance sheet flexibility. Even with strong FCF, the sharp decline in equity amplifies leverage metrics, raising refinancing and covenant sensitivity and constraining optionality for M&A or cushioning against an earnings setback.

Sustained weakness at a major brand lowers consolidated growth and can dilute group margins if recovery requires heavy promotions or investment. A prolonged turnaround will demand marketing and product repositioning, tying up management focus and capital and weighing on multi-brand portfolio stability.

Persistent tariff costs compress margins unless fully offset by price or sourcing changes. Concurrently elevated marketing and SG&A as a percent of sales raise the fixed-cost base. Together these structural pressures can slow margin recovery and make earnings sensitive to external cost or demand shocks.
